fields.meta_title: Podcast Landing Page Builder for Growing Shows | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a podcast landing page from a prompt. See four show examples: guest pitches, a listener mailbag, sponsor inquiries, and a survey.
fields.h1: Build a Podcast Landing Page That Works Between Episodes
fields.hero_description: Get a podcast landing page from one prompt, with your best episode up top and forms for guest pitches and listener questions.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Around Your Show
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the page listeners find and the tables behind it, where guest pitches and sponsor leads wait instead of your inbox.
fields.feature_1:
A page written from your show notes

Describe the show and the episode a new listener should start with. Emergent builds the page and its forms from that prompt, and the next season takes one more prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Listener emails you keep

The app saves every signup to a database you own, along with the episode page the listener signed up on. Change newsletter tools next year and the list comes with you.
fields.feature_3:
Forms for the people around the mic

A guest gives a topic and a past interview link, a listener a question and its topic, a sponsor a spot count. Each answer lands in its own table, ready to sort and search.
fields.feature_4:
A heads-up when a pitch arrives

Pick who hears about each form and where. The app can email your producer about a strong guest pitch or post a sponsor inquiry to a Slack channel as soon as it comes in.
fields.feature_5:
Hooks into the tools you already run

Built apps connect to any tool with an API. New signups can sync straight to your email platform, and sponsor leads can reach your CRM with no spreadsheet between them.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and code on GitHub

Custom domains are included in Emergent for the show's own address. Paid plans export the full code to your GitHub repository, and the free tier covers building and publishing.

fields.tab_content_1:
Ruben gets every pitch that links a sample

Guests pitch The Workbench Hour through a form that asks for a topic and a link to a past interview. The app emails each pitch that includes a sample link to the producer, Ruben Ibarra, and keeps the rest in the pitch table for the host. In May, 17 of 46 pitches went to Ruben and 29 stayed in the table.
fields.tab_content_2:
Before the June mailbag, tomatoes led with 54 questions

Every question sent to Back Forty Garden Hour comes through a mailbag form where the listener picks a topic before typing. Questions are tallied by topic as they arrive. Before recording the June mailbag episode, the host could see that 54 of the 132 questions were about tomatoes, against 41 about soil.
fields.tab_content_3:
Sponsor inquiries post to #sponsors in Slack

Brands that want to sponsor Small Shop Radio fill in a form with the product and the number of ad spots they want. Each inquiry then posts to the #sponsors channel in the team's Slack, where whoever is free picks it up. Tallybook, a bookkeeping app, asked for 6 spots, one of 23 inquiries in the third quarter.
fields.tab_content_4:
289 listeners out of 506 tune in on the commute

Trailhead Radio wanted a hard number for sponsors. The host put a four-question listener survey on the page, and the app saves every answer to the show's database. Of the 506 listeners who answered, 289 said they listen while commuting, and that figure now leads the show's sponsor page.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Podcast Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps take a podcast landing page from one clear action to a tested, live page that keeps every listener and pitch.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask each form for only what you use
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what a first-time visitor should do: play an episode, follow the show, or join the email list. Put that action first and push everything else further down the page.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Your newest episode may lean on inside jokes from the last ten. Pick one that stands on its own, put it on the first screen, and write one line on why it is worth 40 minutes.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Tell Emergent the show name, the starter episode, the follow links, and each form you want. From that description, Emergent builds the page, the forms, and the tables behind them.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask a guest for a pitch and one sample, not a full bio and a headshot. Every extra field is one more reason to close the tab. Cut any question whose answer you will never read.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Name the person or Slack channel for each form. A producer can get strong guest pitches by email while sponsor inquiries go to the team channel.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send a real pitch through the form
fields.howto_step_6_des: Fill in every form yourself, on your phone, the way a guest would. Check that the entry lands in the right table and that the right person heard about it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Share it where listeners already are
fields.howto_step_7_des: Link the page from your show notes, your podcast description, and your social bios. When a better starter episode airs, swap it in with one more prompt.

faq_plan.q: What is a podcast landing page?
faq_plan.a: A podcast landing page is a single web page built to turn a visitor into a listener. It leads with one episode to play, links to follow the show in the listening apps your audience uses, and asks for an email. A stronger one also takes guest pitches and listener questions.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a podcast landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the show, the starter episode, and the forms you need in one prompt to Emergent's AI landing page builder, and it builds the page with the database behind it. Test each form with a real entry before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: Should a podcast landing page lead with the newest episode?
faq_plan.a: Not always. Lead with the newest episode only if a stranger can follow it without hearing the ones before it. For an interview show the latest guest works; for a serialized story, put episode one on top and the newest below it.

faq_plan.q: How do I promote my course from a podcast landing page?
faq_plan.a: Give the course one clear spot on the podcast page, such as a line under the starter episode, and send that link to a separate course landing page. The podcast page earns trust over many episodes; the course page holds the syllabus and the signup, which would crowd the episodes out.

faq_plan.q: Do I need a podcast landing page for every episode?
faq_plan.a: No, but a page for a big episode helps when you promote that episode on its own. The show page covers following and signups. An episode page can carry the guest's links and a transcript. Emergent can add an episode page to the same app with one more prompt.

faq_plan.q: How do I collect guest pitches on a podcast landing page?
faq_plan.a: Use a short pitch form with the guest's name, the angle they would bring, and one recording of them on mic, such as a past episode or a recorded talk. The recording matters most: you hear how a guest sounds before you reply. In an app Emergent builds, each pitch lands in a table you can sort, and an email alert can reach whoever books guests.

faq_plan.q: Should my book share my podcast landing page?
faq_plan.a: No. Keep them on separate pages and link them. A podcast page asks a visitor to press play, while a book landing page asks them to buy or preorder, and one page chasing both goals does neither well. Mention the book under the starter episode and link to its page.

faq_plan.q: What should a podcast landing page show sponsors?
faq_plan.a: Show sponsors who listens, how they listen, the ad formats you sell, and a short inquiry form. Numbers from your own listener survey carry more weight than adjectives about your audience. An app Emergent builds can connect the inquiry form to the CRM you already use through its API.

faq_plan.q: Can I embed a player on a podcast landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The Apple Podcasts embed player, for one, lets you feature your show or a specific episode directly on your website. Look in your podcast host's dashboard for its own player code as well, and test the player on a phone before you publish.

faq_plan.q: Should a real estate agent build a podcast landing page?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the show is how you meet clients. Keep the podcast page about listening and following, and send listeners who are ready to buy or sell to a separate real estate landing page with your listings and a contact form. Each page then has one job.

plan.angle: The top results for this search are guides and host-bundled pages that list the parts of a podcast page (player, episode list, follow buttons, email signup) and stop there. This page shows four shows whose page also collects what a podcast runs on between episodes, each built from a prompt: an interview show's guest pitch form that sends pitches with an audio sample to the producer, a gardening show's mailbag that counts listener questions by topic, a small-business show's sponsor form that posts each inquiry to the team's Slack channel, and a hiking show's listener survey that feeds its sponsor page. It stays on podcasts, leaving music releases to the artist page, and the FAQ covers the build, the starter episode, per-episode pages, guest pitches, sponsor pages, embedded players, and when a course, a book, or a real estate business needs its own page.
